## Adjuvant Trastuzumab Trials in Early-Stage HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

### Overview

In 2005, the simultaneous publication of results from three landmark phase III trials — **HERA**, **NSABP B-31**, and **NCCTG N9831** — transformed the treatment of early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer. All three demonstrated that adding one year of adjuvant trastuzumab to standard chemotherapy produced large, durable improvements in both disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS).

---

### NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831 (Joint Analysis)

These two US-based trials enrolled a combined **4,046 patients** with HER2-positive operable breast cancer. Both used a backbone of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel (AC→T), with or without trastuzumab.

- **NSABP B-31** enrolled only node-positive patients.
- **NCCTG N9831** enrolled node-positive and high-risk node-negative patients and also included an arm evaluating sequential (rather than concurrent) trastuzumab.

At the **planned definitive analysis** (median follow-up 8.4 years):

| Endpoint | Chemo + Trastuzumab | Chemo Alone | Hazard Ratio | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **10-year OS** | 84% | 75.2% | 0.63 (95% CI 0.54–0.73) | < 0.001 |
| **10-year DFS** | 73.7% | 62.2% | 0.60 (95% CI 0.53–0.68) | < 0.001 |

Adding trastuzumab produced a **37% relative reduction in the risk of death** and a **40% relative reduction in the risk of recurrence**. All patient subgroups benefited.

---

### HERA (HERceptin Adjuvant) Trial

HERA was an international trial that enrolled **5,102 women** with HER2-positive early breast cancer and randomized them to observation, 1 year of trastuzumab, or 2 years of trastuzumab, given after completion of adjuvant chemotherapy.

At the **final analysis** (median follow-up 11 years):

- **1 year of trastuzumab vs. observation:**
  - DFS: HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.68–0.86) — a **24% relative reduction** in recurrence risk
  - OS: HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.64–0.86) — a **26% relative reduction** in death risk
  - 10-year DFS: **69%** (trastuzumab) vs. **63%** (observation)
  - 12-year OS: **79%** (trastuzumab) vs. **73%** (observation)

- **2 years vs. 1 year of trastuzumab:** No additional benefit was seen (HR 1.02), confirming **1 year as the standard duration**.

Notably, 52% of patients in the observation arm crossed over to receive trastuzumab after the initial positive results were published, which likely diluted the observed benefit. Cardiac toxicity remained low across all groups.

---

### FDA Approval of Herceptin for Early-Stage Disease

- Herceptin (trastuzumab) was first approved by the FDA in **September 1998** for metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer.
- On **November 16, 2006**, the FDA approved Herceptin for the **adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive, node-positive early-stage breast cancer**, in combination with doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, and paclitaxel (AC→TH), based on the combined interim analysis of NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831.
- In **January 2008**, the FDA expanded the approval to include trastuzumab as a single agent following multi-modality anthracycline-based therapy, and to cover node-negative disease (ER/PR-negative or with one high-risk feature).
- In **May 2008**, two additional trastuzumab-containing regimens were approved, including the non-anthracycline TCH regimen (docetaxel, carboplatin, and trastuzumab).

---

### Impact

These trials collectively established one year of adjuvant trastuzumab as the standard of care for HER2-positive early breast cancer, roughly halving the relative risk of recurrence and reducing the risk of death by approximately one-quarter to one-third. They transformed HER2-positive disease from one of the most aggressive breast cancer subtypes into a highly treatable one.

Median time on study was 8.4 years. Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy led to a 37% relative improvement in OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.73; P < .001) and an increase in 10-year OS rate from 75.2% to 84%. These results were accompanied by an improvement in DFS of 40% (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.68; P < .001) and increase in 10-year DFS rate from 62.2% to 73.7%. All patient subgroups benefited from addition of this targeted anti-HER2 agent.
